pr.title: Accept only colors that look right in panel.background
pr.head: 6a13f502d320af68969374e59d4e374e1e13049a

summary: Projector's panel is the box it draws above Claude Code's prompt, listing tracked pull requests and inbox items. In a terminal the panel sits on a background color of its own. By default that color follows the Claude Code theme, and the panel.background setting in .projector.toml picks another.

Before this change the panel drew any value made of color-like characters. Claude Code treats a value that starts with rgb(, # or ansi256( as a literal color, and looks any other value up as a theme key, a named color in the active theme such as inverseText. A name that is no key, such as the typo inverseTxt, draws no color at all. So a typo left the panel with no background and no warning, although docs/plugins.md promised a fallback.
This change makes the panel accept only an exact list, and fall back to the theme's color with one toast for anything else:

• auto, the default, which follows the theme.
  • A literal color: rgb(r,g,b) or ansi256(n) with each number from 0 to 255, or #rgb or #rrggbb.
  • Three aliases: sidebar draws the theme key composerSidebarBackground, the grey of Claude Code's side panel; black and white draw rgb(0,0,0) and rgb(255,255,255) whatever the theme.
The panel owns the list. The CLI still stores any string, because the plugin and the CLI upgrade separately and two copies of the list could drift apart.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The first commit also offered a subtle alias. A test on that head showed the header, key hint, and ages, all drawn in subtle, vanishing on a subtle background. The second commit drops the alias and refuses subtle.
  • The review of 6a13f50 opened two threads: the comment above BACKGROUND_ALIASES says Claude Code cannot draw a theme key's name, which it can, and one plan line runs past the wrap width.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Theme key: a named color in Claude Code's active theme, such as subtle or inverseText.
  • Literal color: a value Claude Code draws as written, such as rgb(30,30,40).
  • Alias: a short name the panel maps to a color, such as sidebar.
  • Toast: a one-line notice Claude Code shows briefly above the prompt.

groups.title: What the panel accepts
groups.kicker: The allowlist, the literal-color patterns, and the fallback with its toast
intro: The panel reads panel.background through project config get when the session starts and on each reload. backgroundFor turns a value into the color the panel draws, or undefined when the panel does not take it. An undefined result falls back to auto and shows a toast once per distinct value.

The literal patterns are a subset of what Claude Code itself parses, so every color the panel accepts is one Claude Code can draw. Claude Code allows \s? where the panel allows one space, and any number of digits where the panel allows three.

files.note: Replaces the character-class check PAINTABLE with BACKGROUND_ALIASES, the hex and numbered-color patterns, and backgroundFor; readBackground uses it and names the accepted values in its toast.

checks.text: Open review thread: the comment says Claude Code draws another theme key's name as no color, but Claude Code draws any real key, as sidebar → composerSidebarBackground in this map shows. Only a name that is no key draws nothing.
Checked against Claude Code 2.1.299's parser, /^rgb\(\s?(\d+),\s?(\d+),\s?(\d+)\s?\)$/ and /^ansi256\(\s?(\d+)\s?\)$/: every value these patterns accept, Claude Code parses too.
auto is checked before backgroundFor, and a non-string value is refused here, so a number in the TOML file toasts rather than throwing.

files.note: Updates the doc comment on the panelBackground state key: it now holds the color drawn, not the raw setting.
The two panel.background tests now cover each literal at the ends of its range and with the spaces the parser allows, each alias, and a list of refused values that each toast once.
